- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or volatile, model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% or 0.5–1.0 price point to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% or 1–2 price points.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast with upward bias starting from day of sentiment pivot.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate mean-reversion bias; add 0.5–1.0 price point to forecast if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “neutral” or “low” sentiment (0.0–0.3), model often over-optimistically forecasts upward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 price point for next 3–5 days.
